summary.text: Among modules, the free ones are those that have a basis, which is a generating set that is linearly independent.
Every vector space is a free module, but over a ring that is not a division ring there exist modules that are not free.
Many statements true for free modules extend to larger classes: projective, flat and torsion-free modules.

facts.label: A ring over itself
facts.value: It is a free module of rank one

facts.label: Direct sums
facts.value: A direct sum of free modules is free

facts.label: Projective modules
facts.value: They are direct summands of free modules

facts.label: Flat modules
facts.value: Tensoring with them preserves exact sequences

facts.label: Over the integers
facts.value: For finitely generated modules, free, projective, flat and torsion-free coincide

items.prompt: You study vector spaces over a field and call each of them a module over that field. What kind of module is it?

options.label: A module that has no basis
A projective module that is never free
A module that is never generating

items.explain: Every vector space is a free module.

items.prompt: A ring is not a division ring, and you consider all modules over it. What can you expect?

options.label: Some modules will not be free
No module can have a generating set

items.explain: If the coefficient ring is not a division ring, there exist non-free modules, unlike over a field.

items.prompt: You glue together several free modules, either by a direct sum or by an infinite product. Which one is guaranteed to stay free?
items.explain: A direct sum of free modules is free, while an infinite cartesian product is generally not.

items.prompt: A module is described as a direct summand of a free module. What is it called?
items.explain: Projective modules are direct summands of free modules.

items.prompt: Tensoring with a certain module never breaks an exact sequence. Which kind of module has that property?

options.label: A module with no generating set
A module over a field only

items.explain: Flat modules are defined by the property that tensoring with them preserves exact sequences.

items.prompt: A finitely generated module over the integers is flat. What follows about it?

options.label: It is free, projective and torsion-free as well

items.explain: For a finitely generated module over a principal ideal domain such as the integers, the properties free, projective, flat and torsion-free are equivalent.
